Note::contains_any_digit¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::contains_any_digit() const

Test Whether A Cell Has At Least One Digit¶

contains_any_digit() reports, for each cell, whether any byte is an ASCII digit 0–9. It is the “some” counterpart of is_digit’s “all”: use it to flag rows that carry a number somewhere — an ID, a year, a quantity — as opposed to pure prose.

An empty cell returns 0.

Return value¶

A Bool Note with the receiver’s shape, one native truth value per cell. Use bools() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"order 17", "abc", "v2", "", "3.14", "no numbers"});
const auto mask = n.contains_any_digit();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0]

See Also¶

  • Note::is_digit: “every character is a digit”.

  • Note::contains_any_alpha: the letter version.
